after.notes: Checked all three proof steps against the Gaussian-law Definition, Countable Choice and orthogonal Lebesgue invariance Statement. The real-linear Frobenius isometry preserves the radial real or normalized complex product density; factoring transformed entries gives independence of disjoint row blocks. Zero dimensions and empty blocks have deterministic laws, while 1-by-1 transforms and singular Gaussian realizations need no extra hypotheses. Countable Choice is retained for the measure suppliers; no arbitrary-index choice is introduced. HMT section 10.1 and its Theorem 10.5 block setup, and Martinsson-Tropp section 11.4.2, were consulted as context. The local density argument independently covers the complex normalization and empty cases. No item repair is required.
